bihar_raw_news.title: Gandak, Kosi river water levels rise in Bihar following Nepal floods - Newsonair
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 31, 2026 8:58 AM Gandak, Kosi river water levels rise in Bihar following Nepal floods Following severe flooding in Nepal and heavy rainfall in the catchment areas, the water levels in Gandak and Kosi rivers have risen in Bihar. To regulate the river flow, all 36 gates of the Valmikinagar Barrage and 20 gates of the Kosi Barrage have been opened. However, the water levels and discharge of both rivers have declined over the past 24 hours. Meanwhile, amid misleading reports circulating on social media, the Supaul district administration has clarified that the water level of the Kosi River is rising at a normal rate and the Kosi Barrage is completely safe. The situation is being continuously monitored. In view of the possibility of a further rise in water levels, the administrations of West Champaran, East Champaran, Saran and Gopalganj districts have been put on alert.

Women’s University in Bihar A women’s university is a higher education institution that admits women students and may also appoint women to teaching and administrative posts. In the Bihar proposal, the university structure is designed to keep all academic and non-academic positions reserved for women. Women-Centric Welfare Measures The state government disbursed about ₹600 crore through Direct Benefit Transfer to nearly 5 lakh female beneficiaries under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana. The government also announced a plan to spend around ₹20,000 crore by 2030 for the development and economic empowerment of JEEViKA Didis. JEEViKA is Bihar’s rural livelihood programme associated with women’s self-help groups and community-based economic activity. The pact ends a 25-year dispute that began after Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar in November 2000. Sone River Water Allocation The final formula allocates 5.75 million acre-feet (MAF) of water to Bihar and 2.0 MAF to Jharkhand. The total allocation of 7.75 MAF corresponds to the share originally assigned to undivided Bihar under the 1973 Bansagar Agreement. Bansagar Agreement and River Basin Context The Bansagar Agreement was signed in 1973 by Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and undivided Bihar. The Sone river is a major tributary of the Ganga and supports irrigation in the eastern plains of India. Institutional Mediation and Project Linkages The Union Ministry of Jal Shakti mediated the settlement through a committee chaired by the Central Water Commission (CWC). A key breakthrough came at the Eastern Zonal Council meeting held on 10 July 2025 in Ranchi, which was chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Paswan, leader of the Lok Janshakti Party (LJP) (Ram Vilas) and Manjhi, head of the HAM (Secular) are important constituents at the Centre and also in Bihar where BJP has its first chief minister in a coalition government. Both Paswan and Manjhi are powerful Dalit faces in the state for the BJP-led NDA. Manjhi hails from the Musahar community, among the most backward Dalit groups. It has been their case that within the SC category, groups like the Paswans and Ravidas communities have been able to benefit more from the reservation extended to the group as a whole. Over the weekend, Paswan reacted strongly to Manjhi and his son, a minister in Bihar, Santosh Kumar Suman’s call for a review in the existing policies for reservation and for sub-quotas for SCs and STs within the existing reservation. Manjhi and his son said a review was essential so that reservation could benefit the most vulnerable and historically marginalised communities. Suman, the national president of the HAM (S), has said that not a single person from the Musahar community has been able to become an IAS officer. "We are not talking about ending reservation. We are talking about making reservation more just, effective and ensuring that it actually reaches those who are deprived," Suman said, as per India Today . national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has arrived in Bishkek on a two-day visit to Kyrgyzstan. He was received at the airport by Kasymaliev Adylbek Aleshovich, chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. A traditional Kyrgyz dance performance was also organised to welcome him. Mr Modi is visiting Kyrgyzstan at the invitation of President Sadyr Zhaparov for 26th SCO Summit. On the first day of his visit to Kyrgyzstan, PM Modi will hold bilateral meetings with SCO leaders on the sidelines of the summit. He will also participate in several other programmes. Mr Modi will address the SCO Summit tomorrow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will first interact with the Friends of India in Bishkek today. He will then visit the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Park and pay floral tributes at the statue of Mahatma Gandhi. The statue was unveiled by Mr Modi during his visit to Kyrgyzstan in the year 2015. The Prime Minister will also hold bilateral meetings with several leaders of SCO member countries today. These include meetings with the Presidents of Armenia, Kyrgyzstan and Iran, as well as a bilateral meeting with the President of Russia. Mr Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games today. The event celebrates the rich and vibrant cultural heritage of Central Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the 26th Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation tomorrow, the first of September. Vikalp Shukla, Akashvani News, Bishkek.” In his departure statement on Saturday, Mr Modi said he is looking forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, based on “security, connectivity and opportunity”. He also said India will work with SCO members towards a region free from “terrorism, separatism and extremism”. Mr Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games. He said the visit will strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia, deepen its civilisational connect with the region and advance the shared pursuit of peace, stability and prosperity. The summit theme is “25 Years of the SCO: Together Towards Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity. The summit’s priorities include counter-terrorism, regional stability and coordination on cross-border threats. The Bishkek Declaration and other summit texts are expected to be finalised during heads-of-state session tomorrow.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 39 Death toll in Nepal flash flood rises to 794, while more than 2,500 people still missing
national_raw_news.content: Nepal has intensified efforts to free hundreds of people trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects, including the Trishuli-3A site, following Wednesday’s flash floods. Rescuers, including experts from India and China have been attempting to make contact but have so far received no response from inside the tunnel. Hundreds of the 2,500 people reported missing are believed to be employees of Nepal’s hydropower projects. Wednesday’s disaster has killed at least 794 people and more than 2,500 people are missing in Nepal. In Tibet, the official death toll is 16, with 546 reported to be missing, while rescuers are struggling to find survivors. Bodies have been recovered from all eight affected districts of Nepal as rescuers race against time to search for those missing and rescue those stranded. A suspension bridge in central Nepal was swept away today due to a fresh flood in the Trishuli River. The bridge connected Ghyalchowk of Gandaki Rural Municipality-8 in Gorkha district of Gandaki province with Charaudi along the Prithvi Highway. The flood, which lasted for around three hours, swept away the bridge at around 11.30 AM. With the flood washing away the bridge, residents of Gandaki Rural Municipality 7 and 8 have lost their access to the Prithvi Highway. Before this, the devastating flash floods on August 26 had swept away a bridge at Dhawadighat, a little distance downstream from Kathmandu. Locals had been using the Ghyalchowk-Charaudi Bridge as an alternative to the Dhawadighat Bridge.

national_raw_news.title: Odisha likely to receive extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places today 20 mins ago 10
national_raw_news.content: Odisha faces another spell of heavy to very heavy rain today, with the weather system over the northwest Bay of Bengal continuing to influence the state. The IMD has forecast extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places today, with a red warning in force for Bargarh and orange warnings for several districts of western Odisha. The fresh spell comes when parts of Kendrapara, Bhadrak and Jajpur are still recovering from the recent floods, raising concerns of renewed inundation in vulnerable areas. Odisha is facing another spell of heavy rain today, as a well-marked low-pressure area over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining West Bengal-North Odisha coast continues to influence the state. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places, with extremely heavy rain at isolated places. For today, a red warning has been issued for Bargarh, while Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Sambalpur, Deogarh, Angul, Keonjhar, Subarnapur, Nuapada, Balangir and Kalahandi are under orange warning. The IMD says the system is likely to move west-northwestwards across north Odisha and Gangetic West Bengal during the next 24 hours. The renewed rain comes as more than sixty-seven thousand people were still affected by the recent floods in Kendrapara, Bhadrak and Jajpur. The IMD has warned that heavy rainfall could lead to localised flooding, waterlogging and riverine flooding in vulnerable catchments.
